name: Bragg’s X-ray crystal structure analysis
description: William Lawrence Bragg interpreted X-ray diffraction patterns to determine simple crystal structures; work with William Henry Bragg extended the method.

impact.note: A laboratory method of specialists, but it first revealed atomic arrangements, and mineralogy, chemistry, metallurgy, materials science and molecular biology all came to stand on it.

date.basis: Year of the dated publication, or a broad historian-estimated composition interval; no first discovery claimed.

events.statement: Lawrence Bragg published early crystal structure determinations in 1913.

evidence.supports: The historical account dates Lawrence Bragg’s initial crystal structure publications to 1913 following the 1912 diffraction observations.
Bragg recalls his own early structure work and his father’s spectrometer, before joint work began in summer 1913.

contributions.resource: Published the early crystal structure analyses.

evidence.supports: The historical account dates Lawrence Bragg’s initial crystal structure publications to 1913 following the 1912 diffraction observations.

earliest_record.rationale: Dated witness within the inspected evidence; not a global-priority claim.

caveats: The 1913 individual work and the later father–son collaboration are distinct. The initial determination followed earlier diffraction work and was not a solution for arbitrary complex structures.

research.note: Independent review checked the 1913 structure publications and the stated link to Laue’s work; other facets retain their prior status.

links.statement: Lawrence Bragg recalled that his early structure work used Laue photographs and diffraction patterns.

evidence.supports: The historical account dates Lawrence Bragg’s initial crystal structure publications to 1913 following the 1912 diffraction observations.
Bragg recounts studying Laue diffraction patterns and using the Laue photograph method for sodium and potassium chlorides.
